name: Urachal Sinus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Diagnostic Criteria for Urachal Sinus

criteria.description: Presence of umbilical discharge or localized umbilical swelling
Ultrasound or CT demonstrating a blind-ending sinus tract extending from the umbilicus towards the bladder dome without communication
Exclusion of patent urachus or vesicourachal diverticulum by imaging or cystoscopy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical symptoms plus imaging confirmation of a blind-ending urachal sinus tract
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; cystoscopy may be used to exclude other urachal anomalies.

laboratory: Elevated white blood cell count during infection
Positive bacterial cultures from umbilical discharge
imaging: Ultrasound showing blind-ending sinus tract from umbilicus
CT scan demonstrating urachal remnant without bladder communication
other: Cystoscopy to exclude patent urachus or vesicourachal diverticulum

distinguishingFeatures: Continuous communication between bladder and umbilicus
Umbilical infection without underlying sinus tract
Typically in neonates with erythema and purulent discharge

redFlags: Persistent or worsening umbilical discharge despite treatment
Signs of systemic infection or sepsis
Palpable mass suggestive of abscess or malignancy
references: Saxena AK, et al. Urachal anomalies in children: diagnosis and management. Indian J Urol. 2010.
Ashley RA, et al. Urachal anomalies: a longitudinal study of urachal remnants in children and adults. J Urol. 2007.
